Natural_Language: This part prescribes policy and procedures specific to the acquisition and management of services by contract. This part applies to all contracts and orders for services regardless of the contract type or kind of service being acquired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_000_a: Part 37 prescribes policy and procedures specific to acquisition and management of services by contract; P_37_000_b: Part 37 applies to all contracts and orders for services regardless of contract type or kind of service
Validation_Notes: Scope statement establishes universal applicability of Part 37 to all service contracts. Both elements are declarative and conjunctive.

Natural_Language: Service contract, as used in this part, means a contract that directly engages the time and effort of a contractor whose primary purpose is to perform an identifiable task rather than to furnish an end item of supply. A service contract may be either a nonpersonal or personal contract. It can also cover services performed by either professional or nonprofessional personnel whether on an individual or organizational basis.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_001_a: Service contract directly engages time and effort of contractor whose primary purpose is to perform identifiable task rather than furnish end item of supply; P_37_001_b: Service contract may be nonpersonal or personal; P_37_001_c: Service contract can cover services by professional or nonprofessional personnel on individual or organizational basis
Validation_Notes: Definitional section. Core definition (a) is conjunctive with permissive scope (b and c). 'May' and 'can' indicate permissive categories, not mandates.

Natural_Language: When acquiring services, including acquisition of commercial services using the procedures in part 12, agencies must use performance-based acquisition methods to the maximum extent practicable (with exceptions) and use an order of precedence for contract types.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1: Agencies acquiring services must comply with performance-based acquisition and precedence requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for 37.101-1. Combines mandatory PBA requirement with precedence hierarchy. Both subsections apply when acquiring services.

Natural_Language: When acquiring services, including acquisition of commercial services using the procedures in part 12, agencies must use performance-based acquisition methods to the maximum extent practicable, except for architect-engineer services (part 36), construction (part 36), utility services (part 41), or services incidental to supply purchases.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_a_base: Agencies must use performance-based acquisition methods to maximum extent practicable when acquiring services; P_37_101_1_a_exc: Except for A-E services, construction, utility services, or services incidental to supply
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Parent for exceptions. Mandatory 'must' with carved-out exceptions. The requirement applies unless one of four exceptions is triggered. Negation of the disjunction of exceptions accurately represents 'except for' language.

Natural_Language: Architect-engineer services acquired in accordance with 40 U.S.C. 1101 et seq. (see part 36).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_a_1: Services are architect-engineer services acquired per 40 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.
Validation_Notes: Exception to PBA requirement. If services are A-E per statute, then PBA mandate does not apply. HIGH-RISK: Material implication used to model exception. Direction is correct: A-E status triggers exemption, not the reverse.

Natural_Language: Construction (see part 36).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_a_2: Services are construction
Validation_Notes: Exception to PBA requirement for construction services. Same logical pattern as (a)(1).

Natural_Language: Utility services (see part 41).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_a_3: Services are utility services
Validation_Notes: Exception to PBA requirement for utility services. Same logical pattern as (a)(1).

Natural_Language: Services that are incidental to supply purchases.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_a_4: Services are incidental to supply purchases
Validation_Notes: Exception to PBA requirement for incidental services. Self-contained exception with no external reference.

Natural_Language: Use the following order of precedence (Public Law 106-398, section 821(a)): (1) A firm-fixed price performance-based contract or task order. (2) A performance-based contract or task order that is not firm-fixed price. (3) A contract or task order that is not performance-based.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_b: Agencies must use order of precedence for contract types per Public Law 106-398 section 821(a)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for precedence hierarchy. All three levels are mandatory considerations. The conjunction captures that all three tiers exist; the ordering is implicit in the numbering rather than expressible in standard propositional logic.

Natural_Language: A firm-fixed price performance-based contract or task order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_b_1: First precedence is firm-fixed price performance-based contract or task order
Validation_Notes: First tier in statutory precedence hierarchy. Standalone atomic proposition representing the preferred contract type.

Natural_Language: A performance-based contract or task order that is not firm-fixed price.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_b_2: Second precedence is performance-based contract or task order that is not firm-fixed price
Validation_Notes: Second tier in precedence hierarchy. Applies when FFP performance-based is not feasible.

Natural_Language: A contract or task order that is not performance-based.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_101_1_b_3: Third precedence is contract or task order that is not performance-based
Validation_Notes: Third and lowest tier in precedence hierarchy. Last resort when performance-based approaches are not practicable.

Natural_Language: Procedures for performance-based contracts including PWS requirements and evaluation of offeror-proposed standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1: Performance-based contract procedures encompass PWS requirements and offeror-proposed standard evaluation
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition combining PWS requirements and evaluation procedures.

Natural_Language: Performance-based contracts must include a performance work statement (PWS).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_a: Performance-based contracts must include a PWS
Validation_Notes: Parent for PWS requirements. 'Must' creates mandatory obligation. Three subsections detail PWS characteristics.

Natural_Language: The PWS may be prepared by the Government or proposed by an offeror in response to a statement of objectives (SOO) (see 2.101) and included in the contract. While the SOO in a solicitation may be used to guide the development of the PWS, the SOO does not become part of the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_a_1_a: PWS may be prepared by Government or proposed by offeror in response to SOO; P_37_102_1_a_1_b: SOO may guide PWS development but does not become part of contract
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' for PWS preparation method combined with declarative statement about SOO contractual status. The SOO exclusion from the contract is a mandatory rule despite the permissive preparation method.

Natural_Language: The PWS must describe the outcome required rather than 'how' that outcome is to be achieved or the estimated level of effort anticipated.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_a_2_a: PWS must describe outcome required; P_37_102_1_a_2_b: PWS must not describe how outcome is achieved; P_37_102_1_a_2_c: PWS must not describe estimated level of effort anticipated
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' with both positive requirement (describe outcomes) and negative requirements (not describe methods or LOE). Correctly separates affirmative and prohibitive elements.

Natural_Language: The PWS must, to the maximum extent practicable, include meaningful and measurable performance standards. Such standards may be established by the Government or proposed by the offeror.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_a_3_a: PWS must include meaningful and measurable performance standards to maximum extent practicable; P_37_102_1_a_3_b: Standards may be established by Government or proposed by offeror
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' qualified by 'to the maximum extent practicable' creates softened obligation. 'May' for source of standards is permissive.

Natural_Language: When an offeror proposes performance standards in response to a SOO, agencies must evaluate whether proposed standards meet agency needs, identify assessment methods, and incorporate both into the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_b_cond: Offeror proposes performance standards in response to SOO; P_37_102_1_b: Agencies must evaluate, identify methods, and incorporate
Validation_Notes: Conditional trigger: 'When an offeror proposes' activates mandatory agency obligations. HIGH-RISK: Material implication correctly models the 'when...must' structure. All three subsection requirements apply conjunctively when triggered.

Natural_Language: Evaluate whether the proposed standards meet agency needs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_b_1: Agency evaluates whether proposed standards meet agency needs
Validation_Notes: First element of conditional obligation. Evaluation is mandatory when triggered by offeror proposal.

Natural_Language: Identify methods for assessing contractor performance against the standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_b_2: Agency identifies methods for assessing contractor performance against standards
Validation_Notes: Second element of conditional obligation. Assessment method identification mandatory when triggered.

Natural_Language: Incorporate both the accepted standards and assessment methods into the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_102_1_b_3: Agency incorporates accepted standards and assessment methods into contract
Validation_Notes: Third element of conditional obligation. Contract incorporation mandatory when triggered.

Natural_Language: Agencies must not contract for personal services unless specifically authorized by statute (e.g., 5 U.S.C. 3109).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_201_1_a: Agencies must not contract for personal services; P_37_201_1_b: Personal services contracting is specifically authorized by statute
Validation_Notes: Prohibitive 'must not' with 'unless' exception. Converted 'unless' to: absence of statutory authorization implies prohibition. HIGH-RISK: Direction of implication critical. Without authorization, contracting is prohibited. With authorization, contracting is permitted (not mandated).

Natural_Language: Characteristics of personal services contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_201_2: Personal services contract characteristics defined by supervision/control indicators and judgment requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for personal services characteristics. Both definition and indicator guidance apply conjunctively.

Natural_Language: A personal services contract exists when the Government supervises or controls contractor employees, or appears to do so, as if they were Government employees. This type of contract circumvents civil service laws that require the Government to competitively hire and appoint its own employees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_201_2_a_1: Government supervises or controls contractor employees as if Government employees; P_37_201_2_a_2: Government appears to supervise or control contractor employees as if Government employees; P_37_201_2_a_3: Such contracts circumvent civil service competitive hiring laws
Validation_Notes: Definitional: actual or apparent supervision/control triggers personal services classification. Disjunction correctly captures 'or appears to do so.' HIGH-RISK: Implication direction correct -- supervision triggers classification, not the reverse.

Natural_Language: The Government exercising relatively continuous supervision and control over multiple contractor personnel is frequently a key indicator of a personal services contract. However, judgment is required because service contracts often involve interaction with contractor employees--such as ordering and reviewing specific work--that do not constitute the type of supervision or control that would convert a contractor employee into a Government employee.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_201_2_b_1: Continuous supervision and control over multiple contractor personnel is key indicator of personal services; P_37_201_2_b_2: Ordering and reviewing specific work does not constitute supervision or control creating personal services
Validation_Notes: Advisory guidance requiring judgment. The 'however' creates a carve-out where routine contract administration activities are explicitly excluded from the indicator. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW because 'frequently' and 'judgment is required' introduce inherent ambiguity.

Natural_Language: When administering contracts, agencies must avoid making contractor personnel appear to be, in effect, Government employees, unless a statute provides otherwise.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_202_1_a: Agencies must avoid making contractor personnel appear to be Government employees during contract administration; P_37_202_1_b: A statute provides otherwise
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' with 'unless' exception. Absence of statutory exception triggers avoidance obligation. HIGH-RISK: Correct direction -- default is avoidance, exception requires affirmative statutory basis.

Natural_Language: Policy on inherently governmental functions including prohibition, special oversight requirements, and requirement development.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_301_1: Inherently governmental functions policy encompasses prohibition, oversight, and requirement development
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All three subsections are mandatory elements of the policy framework.

Natural_Language: Agencies must not award a contract for the performance of an inherently governmental function (see part 7).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_301_1_a: Agencies must not award contracts for inherently governmental functions
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition with no exceptions stated. 'Must not' creates unqualified negative obligation. External dependency on Part 7 for definition of inherently governmental.

Natural_Language: Service contracts require special oversight if the contract work: (1) Supports an inherently governmental function, or (2) May approach becoming inherently governmental.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_301_1_b_cond1: Contract work supports inherently governmental function; P_37_301_1_b_cond2: Contract work may approach becoming inherently governmental; P_37_301_1_b_req: Special oversight is required
Validation_Notes: Conditional: either trigger condition activates special oversight requirement. HIGH-RISK: Disjunctive antecedent correctly models 'if...or' structure. Either condition alone is sufficient to trigger oversight.

Natural_Language: Supports an inherently governmental function, including contracts providing recommendations, analyses, reports, or similar work products that can influence government decision-making.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_301_1_b_1: Contract work supports inherently governmental function including work products that can influence government decision-making
Validation_Notes: First trigger condition for special oversight. 'Including' provides illustrative examples but does not limit scope.

Natural_Language: May approach becoming inherently governmental because of the nature of the function, the manner in which the contractor performs the contract, or the manner in which the Government administers contractor performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_301_1_b_2: Contract work may approach becoming inherently governmental due to function nature, contractor performance manner, or Government administration manner
Validation_Notes: Second trigger condition. 'May approach' introduces prospective assessment requiring judgment. Three disjunctive causes identified. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW due to inherent subjectivity in 'may approach.'

Natural_Language: Agencies must carefully develop requirements for such work to ensure contracted functions do not expand into inherently governmental functions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_301_1_c: Agencies must carefully develop requirements to prevent contracted functions from expanding into inherently governmental functions
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' obligation tied to the work identified in (b). Preventive requirement during requirements development phase.

Natural_Language: Agencies must actively administer contracts to ensure contract functions do not expand into inherently governmental functions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_302_1: Active contract administration to prevent expansion into inherently governmental functions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Three mandatory postaward administration requirements apply conjunctively.

Natural_Language: Assigning sufficient qualified Government employees to actively oversee contractor work and monitor for potential encroachment on inherently governmental functions, particularly when the work supports Government policy or decision-making.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_302_1_a_1: Agencies must assign sufficient qualified Government employees to oversee contractor work; P_37_302_1_a_2: Agencies must monitor for potential encroachment on inherently governmental functions
Validation_Notes: Dual obligation: staffing sufficiency and active monitoring. 'Particularly' emphasizes but does not limit applicability to policy/decision-making contexts.

Natural_Language: Requiring contractor personnel to identify themselves as contractors when attending meetings, answering government phones, or in any situation where their status might be unclear to the public or Congress, unless the agency determines no confusion or harm would result.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_302_1_b_req: Contractor personnel must identify themselves as contractors when status might be unclear; P_37_302_1_b_exc: Agency determines no confusion or harm would result
Validation_Notes: Mandatory identification requirement with 'unless' exception. HIGH-RISK: Direction correct -- default is identification required, exception requires affirmative agency determination of no confusion/harm.

Natural_Language: Ensuring contractor-produced documents are clearly marked as contractor products or include appropriate disclosure of contractor involvement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_302_1_c_1: Contractor documents are marked as contractor products; P_37_302_1_c_2: Contractor documents include appropriate disclosure of contractor involvement
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive requirement: either marking or disclosure satisfies obligation. 'Or' explicitly permits either method.

Natural_Language: Covered personnel, as used in this subpart, means an officer or civil service appointee, a member of the Armed Services, or a person transferred to competitive service in another agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401: Covered personnel defined as three disjunctive categories
Validation_Notes: Definitional parent. Three disjunctive categories; any one satisfies covered personnel definition.

Natural_Language: An officer or an individual who is appointed in the civil service by one of the following acting in an official capacity: The President; A Member of Congress; a member of the uniformed services; an employee under 5 U.S.C. 2105; the head of a Government-controlled corporation; or an adjutant general under 32 U.S.C. 709(c).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_1: Officer or civil service appointee by one of six specified officials
Validation_Notes: Parent for appointing authorities. Disjunctive: any one authority satisfies.

Natural_Language: The President.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_1_i: Appointed by the President
Validation_Notes: Atomic element of appointing authority definition.

Natural_Language: A Member of Congress.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_1_ii: Appointed by a Member of Congress
Validation_Notes: Atomic element.

Natural_Language: A member of the uniformed services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_1_iii: Appointed by a member of the uniformed services
Validation_Notes: Atomic element.

Natural_Language: An individual who is an employee under 5 U.S.C. 2105.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_1_iv: Appointed by an employee under 5 U.S.C. 2105
Validation_Notes: Atomic element. External statutory reference.

Natural_Language: The head of a Government-controlled corporation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_1_v: Appointed by head of Government-controlled corporation
Validation_Notes: Atomic element.

Natural_Language: An adjutant general appointed by the Secretary concerned under 32 U.S.C. 709(c).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_1_vi: Appointed by adjutant general under 32 U.S.C. 709(c)
Validation_Notes: Atomic element. External statutory reference.

Natural_Language: A member of the Armed Services of the United States.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_2: Person is a member of the Armed Services
Validation_Notes: Second category of covered personnel. Standalone qualification.

Natural_Language: A person assigned to a Federal agency who has been transferred to another position in the competitive service in another agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_401_3: Person transferred to competitive service position in another agency
Validation_Notes: Third category of covered personnel. Transfer-based qualification.

Natural_Language: When essential to the agency's mission, agencies may contract for advisory and assistance services (A&AS) to obtain management and professional support services, studies/analyses/evaluations, or engineering and technical services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_1_cond: A&AS is essential to agency mission; P_37_402_1: Agencies may contract for A&AS
Validation_Notes: Conditional permissive authority. 'When essential' is the trigger; 'may' creates discretion. Three disjunctive service categories available. HIGH-RISK: Implication correctly models condition-then-authority. Tautology not used because 'may' here grants authority to choose among categories, not binary waive/not-waive.

Natural_Language: Management and professional support services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_1_a: A&AS for management and professional support services
Validation_Notes: First A&AS service category.

Natural_Language: Studies, analyses, and evaluations (see 37.402-3 for limitations on evaluative work).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_1_b: A&AS for studies, analyses, and evaluations
Validation_Notes: Second A&AS category with cross-reference to limitations.

Natural_Language: Engineering and technical services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_1_c: A&AS for engineering and technical services
Validation_Notes: Third A&AS service category.

Natural_Language: A&AS contracts must not be awarded for purposes of performing policy/decision-making work, bypassing personnel ceilings, influencing legislation, or obtaining readily available advice.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_2: A&AS prohibited for four specified purposes
Validation_Notes: Parent for four absolute prohibitions. 'Must not' creates unqualified negative obligations. All four apply conjunctively as independent prohibitions.

Natural_Language: Performing work of a policy-making, decision-making, or managerial nature which is the direct responsibility of agency officials.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_2_a: A&AS awarded for policy/decision-making/managerial work that is direct responsibility of agency officials
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition on outsourcing core agency official responsibilities.

Natural_Language: Bypassing or undermining personnel ceilings, pay limitations, or competitive employment procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_2_b: A&AS awarded to bypass personnel ceilings, pay limitations, or competitive employment
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition on using A&AS to circumvent civil service constraints.

Natural_Language: Aiding in influencing or enacting legislation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_2_c: A&AS awarded to influence or enact legislation
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition on lobbying through A&AS contracts.

Natural_Language: Obtaining professional or technical advice which is readily available within the agency or another Federal agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_2_d: A&AS awarded for advice readily available within agency or other Federal agency
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on external contracting when internal expertise is available.

Natural_Language: Agencies must not contract for A&AS to conduct evaluations or analyses of any aspect of a proposal submitted for an initial contract award unless one of three conditions is met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3: A&AS for proposal evaluation prohibited unless conditions satisfied
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Prohibitive default with three exceptions. HIGH-RISK: 'Unless' converted to: if none of three conditions met, A&AS for proposal eval is prohibited. Direction is correct.

Natural_Language: The head of the agency has determined covered personnel with the required training and capabilities to perform the evaluation or analysis are not readily available in the agency or from another Federal agency (41 U.S.C. 1709).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_a: Head of agency determines covered personnel not readily available
Validation_Notes: Parent for first exception. Head of agency determination required plus timing/procedure requirements. References covered personnel definition.

Natural_Language: The head of the agency may consider the associated administrative burden when assessing the feasibility of using covered personnel from other agencies, including time/cost of searching, travel costs, costs relative to acquisition value, and competing demands.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_a_1: Administrative burden considerations for feasibility assessment
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may consider' with four illustrative factors. Disjunctive: any factor may be considered. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW because 'may' creates discretion, not obligation.

Natural_Language: The time and cost associated with searching for suitable personnel.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_a_1_i: Time and cost of personnel search
Validation_Notes: First administrative burden factor.

Natural_Language: Potential travel costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_a_1_ii: Potential travel costs
Validation_Notes: Second administrative burden factor.

Natural_Language: The amount of such costs in relation to the acquisition value.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_a_1_iii: Costs relative to acquisition value
Validation_Notes: Third administrative burden factor.

Natural_Language: Potential competing demands for the personnel in meeting the agency's mission.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_a_1_iv: Competing demands for personnel
Validation_Notes: Fourth administrative burden factor.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must ensure, to the maximum extent practicable, any such determination is made prior to issuing the solicitation and in accordance with agency procedures. Once the solicitation is released, any determination of a need for A&AS support in analyzing proposals for the initial contract award must be made prior to granting the A&AS contractor access to any proposal material.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_a_2_a: CO must ensure determination made prior to solicitation to maximum extent practicable; P_37_402_3_a_2_b: Post-solicitation determination must be made before A&AS contractor accesses proposals
Validation_Notes: Dual timing requirement. Pre-solicitation is preferred ('to maximum extent practicable'). Post-solicitation has absolute sequencing requirement ('must be made prior to').

Natural_Language: The contractor is a Federally-Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC) as authorized in 41 U.S.C. 1709(c) and the work placed under the FFRDC's contract meets the criteria of part 35.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_b_1: Contractor is FFRDC per 41 U.S.C. 1709(c); P_37_402_3_b_2: Work meets Part 35 criteria
Validation_Notes: Second exception to proposal evaluation prohibition. Both conditions must be met conjunctively.

Natural_Language: Such functions are otherwise authorized by law.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_3_c: Functions otherwise authorized by law
Validation_Notes: Third exception. Catch-all for other statutory authorizations.

Natural_Language: The following activities and programs are excluded or exempted from the definition of A&AS.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_4: Three categories excluded from A&AS definition
Validation_Notes: Parent for exclusions. All three apply conjunctively as independent exclusions.

Natural_Language: Routine information technology services unless they are an integral part of a contract for the acquisition of advisory and assistance services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_4_a_base: Routine IT services excluded from A&AS; P_37_402_4_a_exc: Routine IT is integral part of A&AS contract
Validation_Notes: Exclusion with 'unless' exception. HIGH-RISK: When IT is not integral to A&AS, it is excluded from A&AS definition. When integral, it falls within scope.

Natural_Language: Architectural and engineering services as defined in 40 U.S.C. 1102.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_4_b: A-E services per 40 U.S.C. 1102 excluded from A&AS
Validation_Notes: Unconditional exclusion with external statutory definition.

Natural_Language: Research on theoretical mathematics and basic research involving medical, biological, physical, social, psychological, or other phenomena.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_402_4_c: Theoretical math and basic research excluded from A&AS
Validation_Notes: Unconditional exclusion for basic/theoretical research.

Natural_Language: Agencies must ensure A&AS is not contracted for on a preferential basis to former Government employees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_403_1: A&AS must not be contracted preferentially to former Government employees
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition on preferential treatment. 'Must ensure...not' creates mandatory negative obligation.

Natural_Language: When evaluating proposals for initial contract award, agencies must not use A&AS to support evaluation unless the conditions at 37.402-3 are satisfied.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_403_2_cond: Evaluating proposals for initial award; P_37_403_2_req: Must not use A&AS unless 37.402-3 conditions met
Validation_Notes: Nested conditional: evaluation context triggers prohibition unless exception conditions met. HIGH-RISK: Double implication correctly models when-then-unless structure. Cross-references 37.402-3 conditions.

Natural_Language: Performance monitoring in A&AS contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_404_1: A&AS contract monitoring requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent for postaward A&AS monitoring. Both oversight and payment restrictions apply.

Natural_Language: Agencies must administer A&AS contracts with sufficient oversight to ensure prohibited practices at 37.402-2 are not performed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_404_1_a: Sufficient oversight to prevent prohibited A&AS practices
Validation_Notes: Mandatory oversight obligation cross-referencing the four prohibitions in 37.402-2.

Natural_Language: Agencies must not pay for A&AS evaluations or analyses of any aspect of a proposal submitted for an initial contract award unless the conditions at 37.402-3 are satisfied.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_404_1_b: No payment for unauthorized A&AS proposal evaluations
Validation_Notes: Payment prohibition mirroring 37.403-2 but from postaward perspective. HIGH-RISK: If conditions not met, payment prohibited. Correct direction.

Natural_Language: Child care services, as used in this subpart, means child protective services (including the investigation of child abuse and neglect reports), social services, health and mental health care, child (day) care, education (whether or not directly involved in teaching), foster care, residential care, recreational or rehabilitative programs, and detention, correctional, or treatment services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_501: Child care services defined as encompassing ten service categories
Validation_Notes: Broad definitional statement. Enumerates ten disjunctive categories but the definition itself is a single atomic proposition establishing scope.

Natural_Language: Ensure that contracts for nonpersonal child care services include requirements for criminal history background checks on employees who will perform child care services under the contract in accordance with 34 U.S.C. 20351 and agency procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_502_1_a: Contracts for nonpersonal child care must include criminal history background check requirements; P_37_502_1_b: Background checks must comply with 34 U.S.C. 20351 and agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement with dual compliance obligation: contractual inclusion of background checks AND compliance with statute/procedures.

Natural_Language: Agencies must ensure nonpersonal health care services contracts with physicians, dentists and other health care providers include indemnification and medical liability insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_601_1_a: Nonpersonal health care contracts must include indemnification; P_37_601_1_b: Nonpersonal health care contracts must include medical liability insurance
Validation_Notes: Mandatory dual requirement for health care contracts. Both indemnification and insurance required conjunctively.

Natural_Language: To ensure adequate medical liability insurance is obtained, the contracting officer must insert the necessary value(s) in paragraph (a) of contract clause 52.237-7. Agencies determine the value(s) by considering the standard coverage prevailing within the local community for the specific medical specialty, or a higher amount if necessary to protect the Government's interests.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_601_2_a: CO must insert necessary value(s) in 52.237-7(a); P_37_601_2_b: Values determined by local community standard coverage or higher amount for Government protection
Validation_Notes: Procedural requirement. Mandatory clause insertion plus valuation methodology.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.237-7, Indemnification and Medical Liability Insurance, in solicitations and contracts for nonpersonal health care services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_601_3: Insert clause 52.237-7 in solicitations and contracts for nonpersonal health care services
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause prescription. Unconditional insertion requirement.

Natural_Language: Before making award, the contracting officer must obtain proof that the apparent successful offeror will be able to obtain the required medical liability insurance (e.g., letter of intent from a reputable insurer, underwriting approval letter).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_602_1_cond: Before making award; P_37_602_1_req: CO must obtain proof offeror can obtain required medical liability insurance
Validation_Notes: Temporal conditional: pre-award trigger activates proof requirement. HIGH-RISK: Direction correct -- award cannot proceed without proof. Illustrative examples ('e.g.') are not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: After contract award, but before performance begins, the contracting officer must obtain proof that the contractor holds an active policy for the required medical liability insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_603_1_cond: After award but before performance; P_37_603_1_req: CO must obtain proof of active medical liability insurance policy
Validation_Notes: Second temporal conditional: post-award/pre-performance window for active policy verification. Distinct from 37.602-1 which requires proof of ability to obtain (pre-award). HIGH-RISK: Correct direction.

Natural_Language: Contracts for dismantling of buildings, ground improvements, and other real property structures and for the removal of such structures or a portion of them must comply with one of two labor standards statutes. Service Contract Labor Standards (41 U.S.C. chapter 67) apply when the contract is solely for dismantling, demolition, or removal. However, if the Government plans any follow-on construction, alteration, or repair work of a public building or public work at the same location--even under a separate contract--then the Construction Wage Rate Requirements (40 U.S.C. chapter 31, subchapter IV) apply (see part 22).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_1_a: Dismantling contracts must comply with labor standards; P_37_701_1_b: SCLS applies when contract solely for dismantling/demolition/removal; P_37_701_1_c: CWRR applies when Government plans follow-on construction at same location
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex conditional with mutually exclusive labor standards. One of two statutes applies based on follow-on construction plans. HIGH-RISK: Nested implications model the either/or structure. If no follow-on, SCLS. If follow-on planned, CWRR. The 'even under a separate contract' broadens the trigger condition.

Natural_Language: The standard bonding requirements (see part 28) in 40 U.S.C. chapter 31, subchapter III do not apply to contracts solely for dismantling, demolition, or removal of improvements. However, the contracting officer may require the contractor to furnish a performance bond or other security in an amount that the contracting officer considers adequate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_2_a: Standard bonding requirements do not apply to sole dismantling contracts; P_37_701_2_b: CO may require performance bond or security
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Exemption from standard bonding plus permissive authority. 'May' creates discretionary authority (tautology in consequent). CO has unrestricted choice on whether to require bond. Parent for four security purposes.

Natural_Language: Ensure completion of the work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_2_a: Bond purpose: ensure completion of work
Validation_Notes: First purpose for discretionary bond.

Natural_Language: Protect property to be retained by the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_2_b: Bond purpose: protect Government-retained property
Validation_Notes: Second purpose for discretionary bond.

Natural_Language: Protect property to be provided as compensation to the contractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_2_c: Bond purpose: protect contractor compensation property
Validation_Notes: Third purpose for discretionary bond.

Natural_Language: Protect the Government against damage to adjoining property.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_2_d: Bond purpose: protect against damage to adjoining property
Validation_Notes: Fourth purpose for discretionary bond.

Natural_Language: Agencies must structure contracts to carefully balance payment terms and title rights to protect the Government's interests.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_3: Contract structuring for payment/title balance
Validation_Notes: Parent for payment and title provisions. Both structural options and evaluation requirements apply.

Natural_Language: Contracts for dismantling or demolition may be structured so that either the Government pays the contractor for performing the work, or the contractor pays the Government for the right to salvage and remove the resulting materials.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_3_a_1: Government pays contractor for work; P_37_701_3_a_2: Contractor pays Government for salvage rights
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' with two disjunctive payment structures. Either direction of payment flow is acceptable. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW because 'may' indicates discretion.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must evaluate all salvageable property to determine its usefulness to the Government. When property is worth more to the Government than its salvage value to the contractor, the contract must specifically designate it for Government retention. For all other property, which the contractor will own, the contracting officer must determine its fair market value. This valuation affects both payment structure and any potential termination compensation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_3_b_1: CO must evaluate salvageable property usefulness; P_37_701_3_b_2: Property worth more to Government must be designated for retention; P_37_701_3_b_3: CO must determine fair market value of contractor-owned property; P_37_701_3_b_4: Valuation affects payment structure and termination compensation
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-step obligation: evaluate, then conditionally designate or value. HIGH-RISK: Nested implications model the if-worth-more/otherwise branching. The valuation impact statement is declarative but consequential.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provisions and contract clauses for dismantling, demolition, or removal of improvements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_4: Clause prescriptions for dismantling contracts
Validation_Notes: Parent for three clause prescriptions. All apply independently based on their respective conditions.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.237-4, Payment by Government to Contractor, in solicitations and contracts solely for dismantling, demolition, or removal of improvements whenever the contracting officer determines that the Government must make payment to the contractor in addition to any title to property that the contractor may receive under the contract. If the contracting officer determines that all material resulting from the dismantling or demolition work is to be retained by the Government, use the basic clause with its Alternate I.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_4_a_cond1: CO determines Government must pay contractor beyond property title; P_37_701_4_a_req1: Insert 52.237-4; P_37_701_4_a_cond2: CO determines all material retained by Government; P_37_701_4_a_req2: Use basic clause with Alternate I
Validation_Notes: Dual conditional clause prescription. First: CO determination of payment need triggers clause insertion. Second: Government retention of all material triggers Alternate I. HIGH-RISK: Both implications correctly directional.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.237-5, Payment by Contractor to Government in solicitations and contracts for dismantling, demolition, or removal of improvements whenever the contractor is to receive title to dismantled or demolished property and a net amount of compensation is due to the Government, except if the contracting officer determines that it would be advantageous to the Government for the contractor to pay in increments and the Government to transfer title to the contractor for increments of property only upon receipt of those payments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_4_b_cond: Contractor receives title and net compensation due Government; P_37_701_4_b_req: Insert 52.237-5; P_37_701_4_b_exc: CO determines incremental payment advantageous
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause prescription with exception. Trigger: contractor gets title AND net compensation due Government. Exception: CO prefers incremental payment (which triggers 52.237-6 instead). HIGH-RISK: Conjunctive antecedent with negated exception correctly models 'whenever...except if.'

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.237-6, Incremental Payment by Contractor to Government, in solicitations and contracts for dismantling, demolition, or removal of improvements if both conditions (c)(1) and (c)(2) are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_4_c: Insert 52.237-6 when both conditions met
Validation_Notes: Parent for two conjunctive conditions triggering clause insertion. Both must be satisfied. HIGH-RISK: Conjunctive antecedent correctly requires both conditions.

Natural_Language: The contractor is to receive title to dismantled or demolished property and a net amount of compensation is due the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_4_c_1: Contractor receives title and net compensation due Government
Validation_Notes: First condition for 52.237-6. Same factual trigger as 37.701-4(b).

Natural_Language: The contracting officer determines that it would be advantageous to the Government for the contractor to pay in increments (e.g., to encourage greater competition or participation of small business concerns), and for the Government to transfer title to the contractor for increments of property only upon receipt of those payments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_701_4_c_2: CO determines incremental payment and title transfer advantageous to Government
Validation_Notes: Second condition. CO determination of advantage required. Illustrative examples not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: Definitions: Adjusted hourly rate (including uncompensated overtime) is the rate that results from multiplying the hourly rate for a 40-hour work week by 40, and then dividing by the proposed hours per week which includes uncompensated overtime hours over and above the standard 40-hour work week. Uncompensated overtime means the hours worked without additional compensation in excess of an average of 40 hours per week by direct charge employees who are exempt from the Fair Labor Standards Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_801_a: Adjusted hourly rate defined as (hourly rate x 40) / proposed hours per week including uncompensated overtime; P_37_801_b: Uncompensated overtime defined as hours worked without additional compensation exceeding average 40 hours/week by FLSA-exempt direct charge employees
Validation_Notes: Dual definition section. Both definitions are declarative and self-contained. Formula provided for adjusted hourly rate calculation.

Natural_Language: Agencies must ensure solicitations do not incentivize the use of uncompensated overtime (10 U.S.C. 4507).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_1: Solicitations must not incentivize uncompensated overtime
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. 'Must ensure...do not' creates mandatory negative obligation. Statutory authority cited.

Natural_Language: Agencies must not contract with organizations that offer quasi-military armed forces for hire, or with their employees, regardless of the contract's character (5 U.S.C. 3108). An organization providing guard or protective services is not considered a quasi-military armed force, even though the guards are armed or the organization provides general investigative or detective services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_2_a: Must not contract with quasi-military armed forces or their employees; P_37_802_2_b: Guard/protective service organizations are not quasi-military even if armed
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition with definitional carve-out. The carve-out prevents over-application of the prohibition to legitimate security services.

Natural_Language: Foreign national severance cost limitations, waivers, and applicability.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3: Foreign national severance framework
Validation_Notes: Parent for three elements: cost limitations, waiver authority, and applicability determination.

Natural_Language: Part 31 specifies cost allowability limitations for severance payments to foreign nationals under service contracts outside the United States. However, agencies may waive or except the cost limitations in certain circumstances (see 10 U.S.C. 3744 and 41 U.S.C. 4304).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_a_1: Part 31 specifies cost limitations for foreign national severance; P_37_802_3_a_2: Agencies may waive or except cost limitations
Validation_Notes: Declarative plus permissive authority. 'May waive' creates discretionary authority modeled as tautology. Statutory references provided.

Natural_Language: Waivers of severance cost limitations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_b: Waiver authority and restrictions
Validation_Notes: Parent for waiver provisions. Three elements: authority conditions, prohibition, and timing.

Natural_Language: The head of the agency may waive such severance cost limitations when the contract provides significant support services for armed forces or executive agency employees outside US, and the head of agency determines conditions in 52.237-8(b) are present.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_b_1_cond: Contract provides significant support outside US; P_37_802_3_b_1_det: HCA determines conditions in 52.237-8(b) present
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Complex conditional permissive authority. Three conjunctive conditions: (i or ii) AND (iii). When met, HCA 'may' waive (tautology = discretion). HIGH-RISK: Correct modeling of 'may waive when' structure.

Natural_Language: Provides significant support services for members of the armed forces stationed or deployed outside the United States.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_b_1_i: Contract provides significant support for armed forces outside US
Validation_Notes: First alternative condition for waiver authority.

Natural_Language: Provides significant support for employees of an executive agency posted outside the United States.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_b_1_ii: Contract provides significant support for executive agency employees outside US
Validation_Notes: Second alternative condition for waiver authority.

Natural_Language: The head of the agency determines the conditions outlined in 52.237-8(b) are present.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_b_1_iii: HCA determines 52.237-8(b) conditions present
Validation_Notes: Required determination. Must accompany either (i) or (ii).

Natural_Language: Waivers cannot be granted if the severance is a result of the curtailment or termination of basing rights of the United States military at the request of the host government (see part 31).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_b_2_cond: Severance results from curtailment/termination of US military basing rights at host government request; P_37_802_3_b_2_req: Waiver cannot be granted
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition triggered by specific cause of severance. HIGH-RISK: If basing rights curtailment causes severance, waiver categorically prohibited. No discretion.

Natural_Language: Waivers may only be granted prior to contract award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_b_3: Waivers permitted only prior to contract award
Validation_Notes: Timing restriction. 'Only...prior to' creates biconditional-like constraint. If not pre-award, waiver prohibited. HIGH-RISK: Correct direction.

Natural_Language: The Secretary of Defense may determine that the cost allowability limitations on severance do not apply in military banking contracts (10 U.S.C. 3744(a)(13) and (14)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_3_c_cond: Military banking contract; P_37_802_3_c: SecDef may determine cost limitations do not apply
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority limited to SecDef and military banking contracts. 'May determine' = discretion (tautology). Statutory authority cited. HIGH-RISK: Correct use of tautology for 'may.'

Natural_Language: Use of private sector temporaries.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_4: Private sector temporary help framework
Validation_Notes: Parent for three elements: authority/limitations, compliance, and consultation.

Natural_Language: Agencies may hire temporary help service firms to provide workers for short-term or occasional needs (5 U.S.C. 3109). These arrangements are not considered personal services contracts. However, agencies cannot use temporary help to avoid normal Federal hiring processes or replace existing Federal employees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_4_a_1: Agencies may hire temporary help for short-term needs; P_37_802_4_a_2: Temporary help arrangements are not personal services; P_37_802_4_a_3: Cannot use to avoid Federal hiring or replace Federal employees
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority with definitional clarification and prohibitive guardrails. 'May' for hiring, declarative for non-personal-services status, 'cannot' for limitations.

Natural_Language: All temporary help contracts must comply with the requirements in 5 CFR part 300, subpart E, Use of Private Sector Temporaries, and agency procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_4_b: Temporary help contracts must comply with 5 CFR part 300 subpart E and agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Mandatory compliance obligation with external regulatory reference.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers should consult with cognizant civilian personnel offices for expertise when exercising this authority.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_4_c: COs should consult civilian personnel offices
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' indicates recommended practice, not mandatory. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW per modal verb mapping for advisory requirements.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provisions and contract clauses for other service considerations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5: Clause prescriptions for service contracts
Validation_Notes: Parent for six clause prescriptions. Each applies independently based on its own conditions.

Natural_Language: Insert the provision at 52.237-1, Site Visit, in solicitations for services to be performed on Government installations, unless the solicitation is for construction.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_a_cond: Services on Government installations and not construction; P_37_802_5_a_req: Insert 52.237-1
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause prescription with exception. Services on Government installations trigger insertion UNLESS construction. HIGH-RISK: Conjunctive antecedent with negated exception.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.237-2, Protection of Government Buildings, Equipment, and Vegetation, in solicitations and contracts for services to be performed on Government installations, unless a construction contract is contemplated.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_b_cond: Services on Government installations and not construction; P_37_802_5_b_req: Insert 52.237-2
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Same conditional pattern as (a). Services on Government installations minus construction triggers clause.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.237-3, Continuity of Services, in solicitations and contracts for services, when services are vital and transition difficulties anticipated.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_c: Insert 52.237-3 when both conditions met
Validation_Notes: Parent for two conjunctive conditions. Both vitality and transition difficulty must be present. HIGH-RISK: Both conditions required.

Natural_Language: The services under the contract are considered vital to the Government and must be continued without interruption and when, upon contract expiration, a successor, either the Government or another contractor, may continue them.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_c_1: Services are vital, must continue without interruption, and successor may continue upon expiration
Validation_Notes: First condition: vitality and continuity requirement.

Natural_Language: The Government anticipates difficulties during the transition from one contractor to another or to the Government. Examples of instances where use of the clause may be appropriate are services in remote locations or services requiring personnel with special security clearances.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_c_2: Government anticipates transition difficulties
Validation_Notes: Second condition: anticipated transition difficulty. Examples are illustrative.

Natural_Language: Insert the provision at 52.237-8, Restriction on Severance Payments to Foreign Nationals, in solicitations that meet the criteria in 37.802-3(b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_d_cond: Solicitation meets 37.802-3(b) criteria; P_37_802_5_d_req: Insert 52.237-8
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause prescription cross-referencing waiver criteria. HIGH-RISK: Correct direction.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.237-9, Waiver of Limitation on Severance Payments to Foreign Nationals when the head of an agency has granted a waiver pursuant to 37.802-3(b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_e_cond: HCA granted waiver per 37.802-3(b); P_37_802_5_e_req: Insert 52.237-9
Validation_Notes: Conditional on actual waiver grant, not just criteria eligibility. Distinct from (d) which triggers on criteria met. HIGH-RISK: Correct direction.

Natural_Language: Insert the provision at 52.237-10, Identification of Uncompensated Overtime, in solicitations valued above the simplified acquisition threshold, for professional or technical services to be acquired on the basis of the level of effort rather than performance outcome required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_802_5_f_cond1: Solicitation valued above SAT; P_37_802_5_f_cond2: Professional or technical services acquired on LOE basis; P_37_802_5_f_req: Insert 52.237-10
Validation_Notes: Dual conjunctive conditions: above SAT AND LOE-based professional/technical services. Both must be met. HIGH-RISK: Correct modeling of 'in solicitations...for services' dual trigger.

Natural_Language: Agencies must ensure an offeror's use of uncompensated overtime will not degrade the level of technical expertise required to meet Government requirements. When offerors propose uncompensated overtime, contracting officers must assess potential risks.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_1: Uncompensated overtime evaluation requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent for three evaluation methods. All three risk assessment techniques apply when offerors propose uncompensated overtime.

Natural_Language: Using adjusted hourly rates instead of standard hourly rates for all proposed hours.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_1_a: Use adjusted hourly rates for all proposed hours
Validation_Notes: First evaluation method. References adjusted hourly rate definition in 37.801.

Natural_Language: Reviewing whether unrealistically low labor rates or costs might lead to poor quality or inadequate service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_1_b: Review for unrealistically low rates/costs leading to poor quality
Validation_Notes: Second evaluation method. Quality risk assessment.

Natural_Language: Examining whether uncompensated overtime is distributed unevenly across skill levels or concentrated in critical technical positions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_1_c: Examine distribution of uncompensated overtime across skill levels
Validation_Notes: Third evaluation method. Distribution/concentration analysis.

Natural_Language: Funding and term of service contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_2: Service contract funding and term requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent for three funding/term provisions.

Natural_Language: Contracts funded by annual appropriations must not extend beyond the end of the fiscal year of the appropriation except when authorized (see part 32).
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_2_a_rule: Annual appropriation contracts must not extend beyond fiscal year; P_37_803_2_a_exc: Extension authorized per Part 32
Validation_Notes: Prohibitive default with exception. 'Must not...except when' converted to: if not authorized, extension prohibited. HIGH-RISK: Correct direction. Fundamental fiscal law constraint.

Natural_Language: The head of the agency may enter into a contract, exercise an option, or place an order under a contract for severable services for a period that begins in one fiscal year and ends in the next fiscal year if the period of the contract awarded, option exercised, or order placed does not exceed one year (10 U.S.C. 3133 and 41 U.S.C. 3902). Funds made available for a fiscal year may be obligated for the total amount of an action entered into under this authority.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_2_b_cond: Severable services contract period does not exceed one year; P_37_803_2_b_auth: HCA may enter cross-fiscal-year severable services actions; P_37_803_2_b_funds: Fiscal year funds may cover total amount
Validation_Notes: Conditional permissive authority for cross-fiscal-year severable services. 'May' = discretion (tautology). One-year ceiling is mandatory condition. Fund obligation authority is declarative consequence. Statutory citations provided. HIGH-RISK: Correct use of tautology for 'may.'

Natural_Language: Agencies with statutory multiyear authority should consider the use of this authority to encourage and promote economical business operations when acquiring services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_37_803_2_c: Agencies with multiyear authority should consider using it for economical operations
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' indicates recommended practice. Not mandatory. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW per modal verb mapping.
